- When sentiment is high (≥0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.2) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to forecast if sentiment volatility > 0.3.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% if recent 7-day average is >10% above 30-day average.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.5, 0.0, 0.5), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of 3–5 prior days for correction.
